verdicts.evidence: https://api.ftp-master.debian.org/madison?package=podman&text=on (2026-10-09): 'podman | 4.3.1+ds1-8+deb12u1+b3 | oldstable | amd64, arm64, armel, armhf, ...'; 'podman | 5.4.2+ds1-2+b2 | stable | amd64, arm64, armel, armhf, ...'; 'podman | 5.8.6+ds1-2+b1 | testing'; also 6.1.1+ds1-1 in experimental. No bookworm-backports or trixie-backports rows. Raspbian armhf Packages.xz (http://raspbian.raspberrypi.com/raspbian/dists/{bookworm,trixie}/main/binary-armhf/Packages.xz): bookworm 'Version: 4.3.1+ds1-8+deb12u1', trixie 'Version: 5.4.2+ds1-2' (Installed-Size 79973). Raspbian has no backports suites (dists/ lists only bookworm, trixie, forky, *-staging and older releases). archive.raspberrypi.com/debian {bookworm,trixie} main binary-{arm64,armhf} Packages.gz: no podman, conmon, crun, buildah or containers-* package. Supporting packages on Raspbian trixie: conmon 2.1.12-4, crun 1.21-1, passt 0.0~git20250503.587980c-2+deb13u1, catatonit 0.2.1-2.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md, section '## 4.4.0': '- Introduce Quadlet, a new systemd-generator that easily writes and maintains systemd services using Podman.' https://packages.debian.org/trixie/{arm64,armhf}/podman/filelist: /usr/libexec/podman/quadlet, /usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/podman-system-generator, /usr/lib/systemd/user-generators/podman-user-generator, /usr/lib/systemd/{system,user}/podman-auto-update.{service,timer}, man5/quadlet.5.gz. https://packages.debian.org/bookworm/{arm64,armhf}/podman/filelist: only /lib/systemd/{system,user}/podman-auto-update.{service,timer}, with no quadlet binary and no generators. The real Debian trixie arm64 .deb (podman_5.4.2+ds1-2+b2_arm64.deb) contains the symlink system-generators/podman-system-generator -> ../../../libexec/podman/quadlet.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/docs/source/markdown/podman-auto-update.1.md.in: 'the container or Kubernetes workloads must run inside a systemd unit'; 'The registry policy requires a fully-qualified image reference'; 'This unit is triggered daily at midnight by the podman-auto-update.timer'; '--rollback ... rollback to using the previous image and restart the unit another time. Default is true.'; 'detecting if a systemd unit has failed is best done by the container sending the READY message via SDNOTIFY ... Without that, restarting the systemd unit may succeed even if the container has failed shortly after.' Notify=healthy exists in 5.4.2: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/docs/source/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.md: 'setting Notify to healthy will postpone startup notifications until such time as the container is marked healthy'. Caveats from the source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/pkg/autoupdate/autoupdate.go restartSystemdUnit() treats only the systemd restart job result as success or failure ('case "done": ... return nil'). rollbackImage() just re-tags the old image ('To fallback, simply retag the old image and restart the service'). The real timer in Debian's package says 'OnCalendar=daily / RandomizedDelaySec=900 / Persistent=true', so it fires at midnight plus up to 15 minutes, and catches up after boot if a run was missed. Debian's postinst does not enable it (see missed).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/docs/source/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.md line 47: 'options defined in the [Service] table and [Install] tables pass directly to systemd and are handled by it.' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go: line 527 'service := container.Dup()'. Lines 569-576: 'Only allow mixed or control-group, as nothing else works well ... return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid KillMode ...") ... service.Set(ServiceGroup, "KillMode", "mixed")'. Lines 587-595: Quadlet adds 'ExecStop=podman rm -v -f -i --cidfile=%t/%N.cid' and then '-podman rm ...' as ExecStopPost via service.AddCmdline, which appends after the user's own lines. The comment there says 'The ExecStopPost is needed when the main PID (i.e., conmon) gets killed. In that case, ExecStop is not executed but *Post only.' Quadlet also sets 'Delegate=yes' and '--cgroups=split' (lines 618-623), so the container's processes sit under the service's cgroup and systemd's kill covers them. Precision: a user-written ExecStopPost runs BEFORE Quadlet's own '-podman rm' cleanup, and it also runs on every normal stop and restart, including auto-update restarts. [Service] Type= may only be notify or oneshot (line 664: 'invalid service Type').

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/podman/v5.4.2/pkg/systemd/quadlet/quadlet.go lines 664-687: unless Type=oneshot, Quadlet adds --sdnotify=healthy, container or conmon (the default), then 'service.Setv(ServiceGroup, "Type", "notify", "NotifyAccess", "all")' and '// Detach from container, we don't need the podman process to hang around / podman.add("-d")'. It also adds '--rm' and '--replace'. This holds for ROOTFUL Quadlet with host or default bridge networking. Caveats: (1) Rootless: since Podman 5.0, 'The default tool for rootless networking has been swapped from slirp4netns to pasta' (RELEASE_NOTES.md). A rootless container therefore also keeps a pasta helper, plus rootlessport for published ports on bridge networks and the rootless pause process, unless Network=host. (2) Notify=healthy or any HealthCmd: v5.4.2 libpod/healthcheck_linux.go createTimer() runs 'systemd-run ... --on-unit-inactive=<interval> ... podman'. options/health-interval.md says the default interval is 30s. So a full podman process starts on every interval: not resident, but a recurring CPU cost on a Pi 3 that nobody has measured.

verdicts.corrected_claim: One unverified data point: symmatree/coordinator#449 (opened 2026-10-08, still open) reports measurements from an unnamed '414 MiB board' (MemTotal 414.8 MiB). The issue does not state the OS, the architecture (armhf or arm64), the kernel or the Docker version. The figures came from a 1 Hz per-process capture while the payload container was running. dockerd used 39.3 MiB RSS (RssAnon 26,924 kB, RssFile 4,528 kB) and 0 CPU. containerd ('3 procs incl. shims') used 30.5 MiB RSS and 0 CPU. The RssAnon 15,396 kB figure is given for 'containerd', taken 'with the stack paused'. The docker CLI used 42.6 MiB and the compose plugin 28.8 MiB, both only while running. This suggests about 70 MiB resident for dockerd + containerd on a small ARM board at a fresh, low-use state. It is NOT a measurement on a 1 GB Pi 3. RSS on arm64 vs armhf, uptime, image count and the containerd image store can raise it; the x86 figures in RES-02 reach 233 MB PSS after 89 days. Measure on the target before quoting a number.
verdicts.evidence: https://github.com/symmatree/coordinator/issues/449 (fetched 2026-10-09): title 'Replace Docker with podman + quadlet on both device roles: no runtime resident between container starts'. The board is described only as a '414 MiB board'; no model is named, so 'Pi Zero-class' is the researcher's inference. Table rows 'dockerd 39.3 MiB 0 us/s' and 'containerd (3 procs incl. shims) 30.5 MiB 0 us/s'. Resident breakdown from /proc/<pid>/status: 'dockerd: RssAnon 26,924 kB, RssFile 4,528 kB; containerd: RssAnon 15,396 kB, RssFile 4,288 kB'. No PSS reported and no Docker version given. The author is advocating a switch to Podman, so the source is not neutral.

Docker docs source, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docker/docs/main/content/manuals/engine/logging/configure.md: 'As a default, Docker uses the json-file logging driver'; 'By default, no log-rotation is performed'; 'the local logging driver is recommended as it performs log-rotation by default'; 'Existing containers don't use the new logging configuration automatically.' drivers/json-file.md: max-size 'Defaults to -1 (unlimited)', max-file 'Defaults to 1' and 'Only effective when max-size is also set', compress 'Defaults to false'. drivers/local.md: 'By default, the local driver preserves 100MB of log messages per container and uses automatic compression ... 20M default size ... default count of 5'. drivers/journald.md: 'Log entries can be retrieved using the journalctl command, through use of the journal API, or using the docker logs command.' dual-logging.md: for 'local, json-file and journald drivers, there is no difference in functionality' (reading is native, so the dual-logging cache does not apply).

http://archive.raspberrypi.com/debian/dists/trixie/main/binary-{arm64,armhf}/Packages.gz: raspberrypi-sys-mods 'Version: 1:20260914' (the epoch is correct). Both raspberrypi-sys-mods_20260914_arm64.deb and _armhf.deb contain ./usr/lib/systemd/journald.conf.d/40-rpi-volatile-storage.conf, whose content is '[Journal]\nStorage=volatile'. The package changelog shows '1:20250627 trixie: Add journald.conf.d/70-rpi-volatile-storage.conf' and '1:20250919 trixie: systemd: lower volatile storage conf file priority', which renamed it 70- to 40- so that user drop-ins override it. Both versions predate the first Trixie image (2025-10-01), so every Trixie image, 32- and 64-bit, has a volatile journal. Bookworm's raspberrypi-sys-mods 20250930~bookworm ships no journald drop-in. Overriding it with a later-sorting /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/ file, e.g. 50-persistent.conf with Storage=persistent, works because drop-ins sort by file name across /etc and /usr/lib.

missed: podman auto-update rollback is only as good as the restart job result. autoupdate.go v5.4.2 restartSystemdUnit() succeeds whenever systemd reports 'done'. With Quadlet's default Notify=false (--sdnotify=conmon), 'the service is deemed started when the container runtime starts the child'. So a new image that crashes on startup (bad config, failed GPIO or 1-Wire init, import error) is reported as 'updated' and NOT rolled back. For a meaningful rollback the app must send READY=1 itself (Notify=true and sd_notify over NOTIFY_SOCKET after hardware init and a self-test), or use Notify=healthy with a HealthCmd.

Debian's (and therefore Raspberry Pi OS's) podman package does NOT enable podman-auto-update.timer. postinst uses the dh_installsystemd no-enable pattern, 'if deb-systemd-helper debian-installed ...'. Nothing auto-updates unless the timer or service is explicitly enabled or started. If the timer is enabled, it has Persistent=true and RandomizedDelaySec=900, so after a Pi was off at midnight it fires soon after boot.

podman auto-update restarts the unit unconditionally, with no 'is the controller idle' check. If the daily timer were enabled, it could restart the controller in the middle of a mash (the ExecStopPost GPIO reset would switch the heater off, but the recipe run is interrupted). Updates should be triggered explicitly, for example by an operator action while idle, not by the stock timer.

The packaged podman-auto-update.service runs 'ExecStartPost=/usr/bin/podman image prune -f' after every run. After a successful update the previous, now dangling image is deleted, so a manual rollback later, such as after a failure noticed minutes after the update, needs the old image archive kept elsewhere or a second tag that stops it from becoming dangling.

Rootful vs rootless matters for resident processes and NFR-024. Rootful Quadlet with Network=host keeps only conmon and the app resident, and its [Service] ExecStopPost GPIO reset runs on the host as root. Rootless Quadlet adds pasta (the default since Podman 5.0), rootlessport for published ports on bridge networks, and the user-namespace pause process. It also needs lingering and a user manager. Running rootful Quadlet with [Container] User= for the app process is the simpler way to meet non-root plus host-side reset; the researcher has not stated which variant is assumed.

Notify=healthy or HealthCmd= makes Podman create a transient systemd timer (systemd-run --on-unit-inactive=<interval>, default 30s) that launches a full podman process every interval. That is a recurring CPU cost on a Pi 3 against NFR-052 (idle < 10 %); it has not been measured. Prefer Notify=true (the app's own READY=1 plus WatchdogSec= if wanted) over frequent healthchecks.

A volatile journal on Trixie is also size-capped: RuntimeMaxUse defaults to a fraction of the /run tmpfs (journald.conf(5)), so on a 1 GB Pi only a small RAM-backed history is kept. Logs explaining a heater or power incident are lost on reboot or power cut unless persistent storage is enabled with a drop-in (a trade-off against SD-card wear). This applies equally to native, Podman (journald log driver by default) and Docker with the journald driver.
